item.title: Two children drown in Sreepur
item.description:
A child and a teenage girl with speech and hearing impairment drowned in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur on Friday.
The incidents occurred Friday afternoon in Nagar Hawla and South Dhanuya villages under Gazipur Union.
The deceased are Jihad (6), son of Zakir Hossain from Nagar Hawla village and a kindergarten student at Nagar Hawla Government Primary School, and Sweety (14), daughter of Rafiqul Islam from Sakhua village of Trishal upazila in Mymensingh. Sweety had been living with her parents in a rented house in South Dhanuya village.
Locals said that around 12:00 pm, Jihad went to play near a pond adjacent to his home. Family members noticed his shoes by the pond, raising suspicion. With the help of locals, the child was rescued from the pond and taken to Jaina Bazar Al Baraka Hospital, where the attending doctor declared him dead.
In another incident at the same time in South Dhanuya village, Sweety entered a pond with friends for bathing. While trying to save another child accompanying her, she herself went underwater and drowned. A local farmer later recovered her body from the pond after a prolonged search.

item.title: Coast Guard seizes 1,500 liters of edible oil in Chittagong
item.description:
The Bangladesh Coast Guard has seized 1,500 liters of edible oil during a raid in the Patenga area of Chittagong.
In a press release issued on Friday, Coast Guard Media Officer Lieutenant Commander Sabbir Alam Sujon said that a special operation was conducted around 2:00 am on Thursday near Charpara Ghat under Patenga Police Station based on secret information.
During the operation, Coast Guard personnel seized approximately 1,500 liters of edible oil (palm oil), estimated to be worth Tk 2.55 lakh, which had allegedly been illegally unloaded from a vessel without paying customs duties and taxes. The oil was reportedly being taken ashore for illegal distribution in the local market.
However, no one was arrested as the smugglers fled the scene after sensing the presence of the Coast Guard.
Legal procedures regarding the seized edible oil are currently underway.
The Coast Guard official also said that such anti-smuggling operations would continue in the future to prevent illegal trade and smuggling activities.

item.title: Experts express concern over rising cases of heart disease
item.description:
Experts at a seminar on Friday warned of rising heart disease in the country, saying that the disease has been emerging as a silent epidemic.
Every day, numerous individuals across the country are experiencing heart attacks and related complications, said the experts attributing the rise rates of the disease to factors such as unhealthy eating habits, smoking, diabetes, high blood pressure, stress, obesity, and lack of exercise.
Pravartak Sangha, a social organization in Chittagong, organized the seminar titled 'Heart Attack: Remedy and Prevention' at Masterda Suryasen Auditorium.
Doctors, social workers, political figures, and journalists participated in the seminar where symptoms, prevention, and awareness of the heart disease were highlighted. Shri Indu Nandan Dutta, President of Promoting Association, Chittagong, chaired the seminar while Dr Shahadat Hossain, Mayor of Chittagong City Corporation, attended as the chief guest.
Ekushey Padak winning journalist, Dainik Azadi Editor MA Malek inaugurated the seminar.
During the seminar, the speakers highlighted that in the early stages of heart disease, patients may experience pressure or pain in the chest during physical activity. Symptoms may also include chest heaviness, pain spreading to the left arm, shoulder, or jaw, and discomfort in the upper abdomen. Such symptoms are often mistaken for gastric issues or general weakness, they said, adding that such symptoms could be early signs of a heart attack. As the condition progresses, symptoms like excessive sweating, shortness of breath, dizziness, or loss of consciousness may occur, they added.
Professor Dr Prabir Kumar Das, Secretary General of the Chattogram Heart Foundation and former Head of the Department of Cardiology at Chittagong Medical College Hospital presented the keynote, highlighting that accumulation of fat in the blood vessels leading to blockages is a major cause of heart attacks.
As the chief guest, Mayor Dr Shahadat Hossain emphasized that the heart disease is a significant public health concern in Bangladesh, with a rising number of cases in both urban and rural areas. He pointed out that the consumption of excessive beef, including meat, in Chattogram, contributes to the prevalence of the heart disease, as excess fat and cholesterol lead to various health complications.
Other experts, including former Head of the Department of Cardiology at Chattogram Medical College Hospital Professor Dr AKM Manjur Morshed, former Head of the Department Dr Ashish Dey, Cardiologist Dr SC Dhar, and Professor Dr Md Anwarul Haque Chowdhury, also participated in the discussion.

item.title: Farmer left destitute as fire reduces house to ashes in Gopalganj
item.description:
A devastating fire reduced a farmer’s house to ashes in Kotalipara upazila of Gopalganj on Thursday night, leaving the family homeless and causing an estimated loss of Tk 6 lakh.
The victim, Kabul Daria, son of Sakat Daria of Majhbari village, said he was at a hospital with his ailing wife when the fire broke out. “I received the news while at the hospital and rushed home, only to find everything burned to ashes,” Kabul said.
According to the farmer, stored paddy, rice, furniture, cash money, and other household belongings were completely destroyed in the blaze. Local residents and the victim could not immediately determine the cause of the fire.
Sirajul Islam, officer-in-charge of Kotalipara Fire Service Station, said firefighters rushed to the scene after receiving the information and managed to control the blaze, though the house had already been extensively damaged.
Fire officials said an investigation is underway to determine the origin of the fire.

item.title: Thief killed in mob beating in Bogra
item.description:
A suspected thief, Selim Mia (32), was killed in a mob beating after allegedly breaking into a house in Chatua Matalpara village of Majhihatta union in Shibganj upazila of Bogra early Friday.
According to police and local sources, Selim and two accomplices entered the house of Gopal Chandra around 3:00 am on Thursday night. They reportedly held family members hostage at knifepoint and looted Tk 3.5 lakh in cash and about 8.5 bhori of gold ornaments, including jewellery.
When the family screamed for help, locals rushed to the scene and surrounded the house. Two suspects managed to flee, but Selim was caught by villagers. He was allegedly beaten severely by an angry mob and died on the spot before police reached the spot.
Shibganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shahinuzzaman Shahin said police recovered the body and sent it to Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsy.
Separate cases will be filed over the theft and the death. Police said a murder case may also be accepted if the victim’s family files a complaint.
